head: aae87a58d61e4f70bbe8c83c2d10de19f2a0a192
claim: Draft pull requests and pull request body edits no longer start CI, and a push to main runs only the areas the merge changed

target.version: BYOKit CI workflows (ci.yml, dictation-wer.yml) and scripts/ci-changes.ts at the recorded commit

steps.start: A pull request branch that changes only the CI workflow files and the job dispatcher; no package code changes
steps: Read the pull_request trigger types in ci.yml and dictation-wer.yml: opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review, with no edited.
Read the draft condition on the changes job, on ci-ok and on the dictation WER job.
Open the pull request as a draft and read the GitHub run it started: every job is skipped and no runner is used.
Mark the pull request ready and read the run it started: the area-scoped job set runs.
Read the pull request's body edit times against its run start times: no run starts at an edit.
Run the old and the new job dispatcher on five real merges to main and count the jobs each would run.
steps.result: A draft pull request started a run with every job skipped; the ready pull request ran its area jobs; body edits started no run; a push to main now runs fewer jobs than before when the merge did not touch a shared input.

verdicts.seen: I read every section: 2 workflow trigger blocks, 5 dispatcher merges, 1 draft run, 1 ready run, and 4 branch runs with 2 body-edit timestamps. Draft: the run started while the PR was a draft (run 40627052986) shows 'conclusion: skipped', 'jobs 26 skipped', 'executed jobs: 0', and ci.yml's types list has no 'edited'. Body edits: both edits (03:32:01Z) fall after every run start (03:30:12Z to 03:30:30Z), and no run is listed after them, so the edits started nothing. Push to main: new dispatcher counts (12, 28, 20, 32, 32) are below the old 32 on three merges; the two merges at 32 changed all areas, so the full set is consistent. The ready run's 2 failures do not contradict the trigger outcome.
